correctness.rationale: Graph-basis preservation is equivalent to preserving the unsigned graph stabilizer space {(x,Ax)}, since its joint eigenspaces are the graph-basis rays. The stated diagonal-block symplectic equation and local determinants follow. Neighbor pairs force opposite-parity a/e values and distance-two pairs have two common neighbors, forcing their b values equal. Distance-two moves connect each parity class, also allowing the vacuous singleton classes in d=1. The diagonal gives c_v as the sum of neighboring b values. This yields the determinant rw+(d mod 2)st=1, exactly six inverse-transpose pairs in odd dimension and four independent shears in even dimension. On label vectors the linear part is diag(e)+A diag(b), and a Pauli gives a translation. Its diagonal recovers e and each column has a neighbor entry recovering b, so the linear action distinguishes the patterns, with the other bits determined. Every translation occurs, giving the stated orders. The two attached finite verification programs were inspected, not executed; the all-dimensional argument was checked symbolically.

evidence: The 2020 one-copy characterization splits every non-Pauli symmetry of a connected graph into an order-three coset form with b=c=1 and an order-two coset form (order-four lifts) determined by the support of its upper-right bit and the corresponding neighbor sums.

Claudet describes a general equivalence criterion; Wang et al. give a two-copy framework and discuss a Q_3 transversal S in a CSS presentation. Conjugating CSS transversal S back by Hadamards on one parity gives a lower shear on that parity and an upper shear on the other, one of the stated Q_3 patterns, not a competing extra pattern in the same fixed frame.

evidence: In the order-three case of Eq. (32), A_cube^2=(d mod 2)I makes the diagonal condition exactly odd d; the edge condition requires alternate diagonal bits across every edge. Connected bipartiteness gives exactly two choices, both valid.

In the order-two coset case Eq. (35) fixes the lower-left bit from neighbor sums and at distance two requires the two common-neighbor upper-right bits to coincide. Thus this support is one of empty, E, O, or E∪O. For each of these choices the remaining diagonal condition fixes the lower-left bit to (d mod 2) times the opposite-parity upper-right bit; the edge constraints hold since the product of the two bits is the same on both parities. These are exactly the four remaining patterns, including the identity.

The odd group has order six and noncommuting inverse-transpose paired actions; the even patterns are commuting independent shears. The action on the Pauli cosets sends a bare phase label through diag(e)+A_cube diag(b), and every column has an edge, so distinct patterns have distinct linear actions. Adding freely available Z translations multiplies the order by 2^N.

A graph-basis symmetry sends |G> to a graph-basis ray, so composition with the inverse Z translation makes it a state-fixing Clifford with the same symplectic action. Conversely any state-fixing local Clifford normalizes the unsigned stabilizer and permutes all basis rays.
